record.original_question: Let M be a compact 4-manifold, and form the double of M by taking a Kirby diagram of M and adding a 0-framed meridian to each framed component, which yields a Kirby diagram of the double. For the resulting 5-colored graph produced by the paper's construction, can one modify that graph in a standard way so as to create rho3-pairs satisfying the hypotheses of Proposition 9, thereby giving a direct gem-theoretic route to the double?

evidence.quote: A particular case of this problem arises, for instance, in the construction of a gem for the double of a compact 4-manifold. It is known that a Kirby diagram of the double can be obtained, from a Kirby diagram of the manifold itself, by adding a 0-framed meridian to each framed component (see [24]).

Therefore, it may be worth investigating whether the particular configuration of the arising 5-colored graph allows to be modified in a standard way so as to give rise to ρ3-pairs satisfying Proposition 9.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. A 5-colored graph (or gem) is a regular multigraph $\Gamma$ of degree 5 whose edges are properly colored by the set $\Delta_4=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, used to encode a closed (or compact, with boundary) PL 4-manifold $|K(\Gamma)|$ via the standard construction that associates to $\Gamma$ a colored simplicial complex $K(\Gamma)$. For each pair of distinct colors $\{i,j\}\subset\Delta_4$, the connected components of the subgraph of $\Gamma$ induced by edges of colors $i$ and $j$ are called $\{i,j\}$-residues.

Compact PL 4-manifolds $M$ admit Kirby diagrams: framed links in $S^3$ (with possibly dotted unknotted components representing 1-handles). The double of $M$, denoted $D(M)=M\cup_{\partial M}\overline{M}$, has a Kirby diagram obtained from a Kirby diagram of $M$ by adding, to each framed component $L_i$, a 0-framed meridian $m_i$ of $L_i$ (and leaving dotted components untouched).

There is a known algorithm $K\mapsto \Gamma(K)$ producing, from a Kirby diagram $K$ of a compact PL 4-manifold $M$, a 5-colored graph $\Gamma(K)$ which is a gem of $M$. 

Define a $\rho_3$-pair in a 5-colored graph $\Gamma$ to be a pair of edges $\{e,e'\}$ of the same color $c\in\Delta_4$ such that $\{e,e'\}$ are joined by exactly three distinct $\{c,j\}$-residues (one for each $j\in\Delta_4\setminus\{c\}$), each of which is a bicolored cycle of length two containing both $e$ and $e'$. A standard "$\rho_3$-move" cancels such a pair, producing a smaller gem of the same represented PL 4-manifold. Suppose Proposition 9 below is given:

Proposition 9 (assumed). If a 5-colored graph $\Gamma$ contains a configuration of $\rho_3$-pairs satisfying suitable compatibility hypotheses, then $\Gamma$ can be modified by a finite sequence of $\rho_3$-moves into a gem of a prescribed PL 4-manifold.

Question. Let $M$ be a compact PL 4-manifold with Kirby diagram $K$, and let $K'$ be the Kirby diagram of the double $D(M)$ obtained from $K$ by adding a 0-framed meridian to each framed component of $K$. Consider the 5-colored graph $\Gamma(K')$ produced by the algorithm above. Does $\Gamma(K')$ admit a canonical, standard modification creating $\rho_3$-pairs that satisfy the hypotheses of Proposition 9, thereby yielding a direct gem-theoretic construction of a gem of $D(M)$ from $\Gamma(K)$?
artifact.category_tag: Gems and Kirby diagrams of PL 4-manifolds
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a future research direction in a 2025 survey on relationships between Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds, and no published resolution was found. Subsequent related work (e.g., on estimating trisection genus via gem theory) does not address this specific construction of a gem of the double via ρ3-pairs.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Original results also appear ... together with open problems and further possible applications to the study of compact PL 4-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed among open problems concerning the gem-theoretic construction for compact PL 4-manifolds.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams and 5-colored graphs representing compact 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm producing a 5-colored graph from a Kirby diagram of a compact 4-manifold.
status_evidence.claim: The base algorithm Γ(K) producing a gem from a Kirby diagram exists, but no direct ρ3-pair-based doubling construction is given.

status_evidence.title: Estimating trisection genus via gem theory
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent gem-theoretic work focused on trisection genus estimates.
status_evidence.claim: Recent follow-up work does not resolve the doubling question via ρ3-pairs.
